thread:
Kai: Quick follow-up from the DR postmortem — putting a single action-tracker here so we can close items before the next game day. Please react with :white_check_mark: when you accept ownership.

Marta: ack, I can take routing policy + runbook edits.

Ben: ack, I’ll own backups verification and the restore checklist updates.

Ash: I can help with the playbook automation and runbook testing.

Kai: Thanks. TL;DR of recurring patterns we saw: BGP session flaps causing split-brain of regional routing, stale S3 lifecycle settings interfering with incremental backups, and unclear restore steps for Dedicated nodes.

Priya: noted — we should also add a checklist item to verify KMS key access during restores. I saw a denied KMS event in the logs.

Kai: Action items (short):
1) Update multi-region routing policy + failover window (owner: Marta) — change desired: failover < 45s with path preference and health-check gating. Due: 2026-04-10.
2) Add explicit BGP session monitoring + alert (owner: Ash) — healthcheck + auto-notify channel + link to netdiag. Due: 2026-03-30.
3) Nightly backup-restore test job (owner: Ben) — small recovery into test VPC using latest snapshot, validate app-level writes. Cron: `0 3 * * *` (UTC). Due: 2026-03-28.
4) Restore runbook rewrite (owner: Ben + Ash) — make a short quick-run checklist (<= 10 steps) and a full playbook. Include expected time-to-restore estimates. Due: 2026-04-05.
5) KMS access preflight in runbook (owner: Priya) — add test commands and fallback KMS contact. Due: 2026-03-25.
6) Post-failover traffic-shift canary (owner: Marta) — script to shift 5% traffic for 10m and validate health before full cutover. Due: 2026-04-12.
7) Quarterly DR game day schedule (owner: Kai) — propose dates and invite cross-team. Due: 2026-03-22.

Marta: For item 1 — draft routing policy (BGP + app-layer) below. Please review and thumbs-up if OK: 
```
# prefer us-west primary, fallback eu-west, then ap-south
set bgp local-preference 200 for route-filter 10.0.0.0/8
route-map PREFER_US_WEST permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list US_WEST
 set local-preference 200
! health-check: /healthz on /routing-proxy -> must be 200 for 3 consecutive checks
```
Ash: lgtm but prefer we tie the health-check gating to both proxy and mesh control-plane. Also add a 30s probe interval.

Ben: For the nightly restore job — I'll use an isolated test VPC and a synthetic workload. Expect ~45m run time for full validation, but will add a smoke-check for quick signal (~8m).

Priya: KMS check snippet I propose: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://test.enc --key-id alias/redwood-main` — return 0 means OK. Add this near top of the quick-run checklist.

Kai: Good. Please update the shared spreadsheet tracker (link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/dr-playbook) with the owner + due date after you accept.

deploy-bot: New runbook created: `DR/restore_quick_checklist.md` by Ben at 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z

Marta: Quick note on rollouts — when we change routing preference we should allow a 2-hour canary window with automatic rollback if error-rate > 1.5% or p95 latency doubles.

Ash: I’ll add the alert thresholds to the runbook and the PagerDuty escalation for SRE on-call.

Ben: I scheduled the nightly restore job to start in staging tomorrow at 03:00 UTC and will post results in #incidents.

Kai: Game day cadence — proposing Apr 15 (dry-run) and Jul 15 (full). Cross-team required: Eng, SRE, Networks, Product. Who’s in?

Marta: in.

Ben: in.

Priya: in.

Ash: in.

Kai: Great. Final ask: any blockers to your owners completing items by the due dates? If none, :white_check_mark: on the tracker. We’ll revisit in 1 week in #incidents.

Marta: no blockers from infra side, might need ~2 devs for canary scripting next week.

Ben: need one access window to run a full restore in prod-like config; I’ll coordinate with Security.

Priya: will add KMS fallback contact to runbook today.

Kai: Thanks all — closing this thread for updates, please open a follow-up thread if you hit any roadblocks.
